description: Team full of coders from Shenners
summary: We developed an application using PySide6 in Python. This application displays data semi-interactively in order to convey to the public how Climate Change is affecting our planet. We wrote a python script that converts SAR data into visualisations that is public friendly, which is embedded in an app. This is important as it demonstrates to the public of how urgent it is for them to take part in Net Carbon Emission objectives (e.g. using paper instead of plastic and not using petrol cars).
details: The Python script parses SAR data from NASA and Canadian Space Agency teams, and formats them into graphs using Matplotlib python module. It then embeds the graphs into the python GUI PySide6. Ultimately, this creates an application where users can click buttons and even use sliders to show graphs and images of the effects of climate change. The benefits is that it shows complicated SAR data into an easy format so the general public can make inferences on it, and thus improve their life to be more eco-friendly, which will be the intended impact. To build the project, we used the python coding language as it is the best language for data visualisation, and my team is more experienced in python than other languages. We also used VSCode as an IDE, and with it, Github Copilot in order to troubleshoot problems and to debug code, nothing more nothing less. We considered the 2 day constraint, which lead us to only use 3 datasets, we acknowledged our proficiency in python, which lead us to use PySide6 as a GUI, and finally, we considered the intended impact of our software and if it is to be used for Samaritan things, in which we pivoted our focus into warning the public about climate change.
dataRefs: Global Annual PM2.5 Grids from MODIS, MISR, SeaWiFS and VIIRS Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD), 1998-2022, V5.GL.04
